correctness.rationale: A uniform permutation factors bijectively as a uniform word of child labels of the prescribed multiplicities and independent uniform permutations within the children. Union greedy decisions are independent in those child permutations, and every maximal independent set is a product of child maximal independent sets. At a join the first letter is i with probability n_i/n; the first accepted vertex blocks all other children, leaving the independent uniform order in child i. Every maximal independent set at a nonempty join belongs to a unique child and is maximal within it. The flat law selects these children with weights m_i/m; within each, the law is flat. Comparing conditional laws and those two child-weight vectors gives exactly the positive n_i/m_i balance condition. At unions flatness is equivalent to flat marginals, which are the independent child laws. The base case is a leaf (the stated construction starts from single vertices). Multiplication/summation of counts and cross-multiplication for balance take a constant number of arithmetic operations per child edge, not necessarily constant bit complexity. This also makes clear which output is given exactly without listing every set.
correctness.reproduction: Read VERIFICATION.md, verification_output.txt and artifacts/verify.py; the frozen order-1 through order-6 exhaustive report is recorded evidence, not a fresh replay. Independent direct permutation counts on K2 joined to an independent pair gave 6,6,12 out of 24 orders, as predicted. The universal proof uses the shuffle bijection and induction, not finite enumeration.

evidence: In multipartite graphs each part has m_i=1, so greedy join weights are the previously known size weights. For a clique bouquet the singleton hub competes with M vertices and P equally likely blade transversals, so join balance reduces to P=M, as its later record states.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior laws cover those restrictions; they do not give an iff condition for arbitrary alternating nested unions and joins. A general first-vertex recursion on arbitrary graphs does yield the join mixture once the blocked complement is identified, but it does not by itself give the cograph no-enumeration uniformity characterization.

evidence: Choosing the next vertex uniformly from currently unblocked vertices has the same terminal law as random permutation greedy, by restriction of a uniform order to the allowed vertices. Proposition 3.8 of arXiv:2608.07239v1 gives a regular-independent-sets sufficient condition, not an iff theorem. At the flat law on a join the child weights are m_i/m, versus the greedy weights n_i/n.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The sampling formulations are equivalent, so the earlier sufficient condition is genuine overlap, not a different model. For K2 joined to two disjoint copies of K2 the exact probabilities are all 1/6 although the graph has degrees 5 and 3, violating the prior condition already at singleton sets.

The later bouquet balance is exactly this test with M=sum blade sizes and P=product blade sizes, for one specific cotree.

originality.rationale: The law coincides with independently stated exact laws on several subclasses and with a known sufficient criterion where that criterion applies, but the exact all-cograph cotree law and iff test are not covered by the compared statements. The probability recurrences are natural decomposition facts; their novel use here is a complete decision and probability rule on the whole hereditary class, including uniform graphs outside the older sufficient criterion.
residual_risks: A modular-decomposition or folklore formulation may imply the full criterion; the recognized cotree primary source was not available for body inspection.
Same-date catalogue labels do not establish priority; limited earlier and later specializations are counted as overlaps to their actual scope.

value.rationale: This gives a complete iff decision and exact individual-output laws across a canonical hereditary class without enumerating maximal sets to test uniformity. Comparing counts and vertex masses gives structural insight not captured by the old sufficient condition or by output-size statistics: K2 joined to two disjoint K2s is irregular and uniform despite outputs of different cardinalities. The short decomposition proof yields an exact algorithm on an unrestricted class rather than a tabulated case.
